Definition: Integration with national payment systems for government-to-person (G2P), government-to-business (G2B) transactions via data exchange
Comments: The Central Bank of Libya regulates some digital payment services. The Marriage Facilitation Fund is cited as a successful e-government example involving banking. However, no cross-government data exchange integrating payments systems is documented.

Definition: Integration of statistics, census data, administrative data for planning, M&E, and evidence-based policymaking
Comments: The GIA is the national statistics and planning authority. The UNDP-GIA MoU (July 2025) focuses on strengthening national data systems for the 7th National Human Development Report. The LY-GOVREP platform connects 60 government entities for reporting. This represents early integration of planning data, though not a full data exchange system.

Comments: The National Telecommunications and Informatics Strategy 2023-2027 exists (GIA referenced it for root server deployment). However, a detailed data exchange implementation roadmap with phases and milestones is not confirmed as publicly available.

Definition: Whether a formal strategy or policy document exists specifically for government data exchange and interoperability
Comments: The National Committee for Digital Transformation was established in 2022 and is developing a digital strategy with a target for implementation by 2030. The GIA's remit includes digital transformation strategy. References to 'national interoperability framework' and 'cross-government architecture' appear in academic analysis and policy discourse, but a formally adopted comprehensive strategy document is not yet confirmed publicly.

Definition: Current operational status of the data exchange system
Comments: No cross-government interoperability or data exchange platform is operational. The General Information Authority (GIA) launched the preliminary operation of LY-GOVREP (government reports platform) in July 2025 with 60 government entities, but this is a reporting/transparency tool rather than a data exchange layer. The National Committee for Digital Transformation (est. 2022) is developing a broader digital strategy.

Definition: Extent to which the data exchange enables services accessible to all population groups including persons with disabilities, elderly, low literacy
Comments: No operational data exchange system. Digital literacy is low among citizens and officials. Limited and unreliable rural connectivity documented. No accessibility standards for data exchange services found.

Definition: Provisions ensuring national control over government data and protecting against unauthorized foreign access
Comments: Libya enacted Law No. 6/2022 on Electronic Transactions including data protection provisions, and Law No. 5/2022 on Combating Cybercrime. The National Telecommunications and Informatics Strategy 2023-2027 references digital sovereignty. Root servers were launched in 2025 to enhance digital sovereignty. However, the legal framework remains partially implemented and no standalone data protection authority exists.

Definition: Extent to which provincial/state and local governments participate in the data exchange
Comments: No data exchange platform exists operationally. Libya's fragmented governance structure (parallel administrations) makes sub-national coordination especially challenging. The LY-GOVREP platform covers central government entities only.

Comments: Libya's digital infrastructure is primarily concentrated in urban areas. Limited rural connectivity and outdated telecommunications documented. No rural data exchange programs exist.
